summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex history of sclerosing mesenteritis, chronic partial small bowel obstruction, and gastrostomy dependence was admitted for increased abdominal pain and bilious vomiting. Imaging showed slightly worsened dilation of proximal small bowel loops, consistent with her chronic condition. She was managed conservatively with bowel rest, IV fluids, and her established pain protocol using IV Dilaudid and Phenergan. Surgery recommended no intervention. She tolerated a trial of oral intake, her symptoms improved, and she was discharged home in stable condition. All home medications were continued without changes, and she was advised to follow up regarding her G-tube size. TPN was resumed at discharge.
